evidence: Shared-state structure: test.sh:104-113 starts ONE app process and DB; run_suite gates (render, constraints) then scored (functional, polish, visual) all hit it sequentially (--max-concurrent-agent 1, test.sh:207). Functional is mode=individual (functional/judge.toml:3), so each criterion session sees only its own criterion text (functional/prompt.md:11). Mutations: gate constraints and every scored global gate add a card to seeded Data Analyst Applied (constraints/judge.toml:25; functional/prompt.md:15; polish/prompt.md:11; visual/prompt.md:11); functional criteria open many suffixed jobs, send messages in Noor's PE conversation (hro_intake_restart, hro_long_thread), add Tomas-email cards (hro_messaging, hro_unread_seen, hro_candidate); polish sends in Noor's PE conversation and leaves drafts. MOSTLY STATE-RELATIVE (good): app_context.md:29-31 'Other reviews may have added jobs, cards and messages; never rely on a starting count'; functional/prompt.md:21 Shared state section (own suffixed jobs/cards, never move records you did not create, relative reads in the Product Designer fallback); hro_long_thread 'earlier sessions may have added messages to it; read counts relative'; hro_messaging/hro_unread_seen fallbacks 'counts relative to their values before you act'; hro_candidate lists statuses with 'including' so extra Tomas applications are tolerated; hro_intake_restart compares post-restart against its own recorded pre-restart values and 'the seeded jobs appear once' tolerates added jobs; polish/prompt.md:14 'If a message or note box already holds text from an earlier review, record it and clear it' and polish/prompt.md:24 'Never use Lena Fischer's conversation'; visual is read-only (visual/prompt.md:14 'Do not move cards or send messages'). Seeded facts quoted by criteria (PE board order and Noor's note in hro_intake_restart; Noor PE Interviewing, Noor PD Application received, Tomas DA In review in hro_candidate) are protected because no prompt moves or annotates seeded cards ('never move records you did not create'). DEFECT: hro_unread_seen (functional/judge.toml:121) grades a pristine seeded value: 'read her unread count on her Product Designer conversation; the starting read markers give her 1. No other session opens Lena's conversation.' with Bar 'Lena's count is 1.' That reservation is enforced only in polish (polish/prompt.md:24); it is absent from functional/prompt.md and app_context.md (grep 'Never use Lena' hits only polish). Because functional runs mode=individual, the hro_readonly_roles session never sees hro_unread_seen's text, yet hro_readonly_roles (functional/judge.toml:94) tells the judge as Rafael to perform 'one conversation read (open any conversation) and one message send (a suffixed message in that conversation)'. hireops_rules.md:136 'Every recruiter reads and writes in every conversation', so Rafael can legitimately send in Lena's APP-301 conversation; per hireops_rules.md:157-158 that message is unread for Lena, so her count becomes 2. hro_readonly_roles is listed before hro_unread_seen and individual sessions run sequentially, so a correct app can then fail hro_unread_seen (weight 3.5 of 61 functional). Nothing steers the judge away from Lena's conversation; a conforming app may list conversations in any order (golden threads.js:38 sorts by latest message; alphabetical or by-job order is equally valid). Secondary P3 notes: (a) hireops_rules.md:181 'Where drafts are kept is up to you' allows server-side per-user drafts; hro_messaging step (3) leaves an unsent reply in 'another conversation' (could be Noor's PE) and polish leaves drafts there, but functional hro_long_thread ('type an unfinished reply ... the reply still reads exactly what was typed') lacks polish's 'record it and clear it' clause, so a leftover draft could be misread as draft corruption; (b) the hro_unread_seen fallback bar 'Mei's count equals the messages in it not written by her (she has not opened it)' is not relative when the seeded Data Analyst conversation is used: Mei has seed read_count 1 on APP-201 and hro_messaging's fallback makes her write there (sending counts as reading); fallback-only, triggered by a defect hro_candidate already grades; (c) polish live-board 'move one other card of the job to Screen' in the Product Designer fallback does not say 'your own card', so a seeded PD card (Noor's, graded 'Application received' in hro_candidate) could be moved; fallback-only. No configured judge run exists (raw-evidence-index.json scope: 'Full configured grading ... absent'), so cross-session interference is unmeasured; run_verdict NOT EXERCISED.
counterexample: Conforming app lists conversations alphabetically by candidate name or by job and implements unread exactly per hireops_rules.md:157-160. The hro_readonly_roles session (told 'open any conversation' and send a suffixed message in it) picks Lena Fischer's Product Designer conversation and sends as Rafael, which is allowed ('Every recruiter reads and writes in every conversation'). The later hro_unread_seen session signs in as Lena and correctly reads unread 2; bar 'Lena's count is 1' fails, and that session is told 'No other session opens Lena's conversation', so the judge has no basis to attribute the 2 to earlier-session state. A correct app loses 3.5/61 functional weight, while a broken app that never counts recruiter messages as unread for candidates would read 1 and pass that leg.
suggested_fix: Add 'Never open, read or write in Lena Fischer's conversation; one criterion reserves it' to functional/prompt.md Shared state (and app_context.md), and make hro_readonly_roles name Noor Haddad's Platform Engineer conversation or its own new card's conversation for its read and send; optionally copy polish's 'record it and clear it' draft clause into functional and make the hro_unread_seen fallback Mei leg relative to her count before you act.
